title: C115 — Ignition coil-on-plug 5
introduction:
An ignition coil produces the high voltage that allows a spark plug to fire. With coil-on-plug ignition, the coil is positioned at its spark plug. This reference helps you understand the connector's assigned circuits and read the identifiers for its listed pigtail service parts.

I begin with the connector identity table, then use each cavity label to find the matching circuit row. The drawing gives the position; the Function column gives the job. That distinction keeps a familiar-looking plastic shell from becoming a guessing game. Read the circuit map before moving to the pigtail table, where kit numbers, service parts and engineering shells have separate roles.

This page is a connector-reading guide. Access, physical viewing direction, probing, wire selection and replacement require matching vehicle service information. Size and gauge conventions are left as printed; the reference provides no electrical test limits or basis for declaring a coil faulty.

edits.why: The printed drawing stacks the cavity labels vertically and shades the middle circle. I pair that shaded position with the unused middle row in the circuit table. The outline and labels help navigate this illustration, but they do not establish the physical viewing side or where the connector sits on the engine.

Read across a Cavity row to preserve the association between circuit identity, color, gauge, function and terminal. The upper drawn cavity maps to powertrain control; the lower one maps to the fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply. The middle cavity has no assigned circuit. This separates the housing's nominal pin capacity from the connections actually assigned in the table.

Each row links the kit Number with its Service Part, Engineering Shell and listed attributes. I keep those labels distinct because a housing identifier and a service-item identifier answer different questions. A shared shell does not settle kit choice or prove interchangeability; replacement and splicing instructions are outside this reference.
